recognition/s594_Longest_Harmonious_Subs.title: Longest Harmonious Subsequence
recognition/s594_Longest_Harmonious_Subs.summary: The candidate proposes sorting the array first, then using a variable-size sliding window where the right pointer advances and the left pointer shrinks only when the max-min difference exceeds 1, tracking the maximum window size encountered.
recognition/s594_Longest_Harmonious_Subs.answer:
The question doesn't specify whether we can sort or not, and sorting is the simplest solution i can think of right now:

[1,3,2,2,5,2,3,7]

becomes

[1,2,2,2,3,3,5,7]

Now it can be a sliding window problem. The right pointer runs, and if the difference between min and mix become more than 1, the left pointer goes in a while loop until the diff between min and max are back to 1. And we record the maximum right - left + 1 we encountered.

There are likely more optimial solutions in O(n) but i can't think of one right now.
recognition/s594_Longest_Harmonious_Subs.why: Sort then variable sliding window tracking max-min<=1 window length is a standard accepted O(n log n) solution to LeetCode 594 Longest Harmonious Subsequence.

The simpliest solution here is to build two sets, s1s which holds each word in s1, and s2s which holds every word in s2 (easy enough to split the strings in python with .split()).

Then one can simply take the intersection of both sets with s1s ^ s2s. That is the solution.
